course.title: Web Development: The Beginner's Journey
course.description: A perfectly structured 27-part beginner course covering HTML fundamentals, CSS styling & layouts, and browser JavaScript for interactive web pages. No prior experience required. Build real skills block by block.

blocks.value: The Internet, Browsers, DNS, and HTTP

Before writing code, understand the pipeline. When you type `google.com` into a browser, your computer asks a **DNS (Domain Name System)** server to translate that name into an **IP Address** (like `142.250.190.46`). Then your browser sends an **HTTP Request** to that address. The server responds with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files that the browser renders into a visual page.

# Step 1: Browser asks DNS for IP of example.com # Step 2: DNS returns 93.184.216.34 # Step 3: Browser sends an HTTP GET request GET /index.html HTTP/1.1 Host: example.com # Step 4: Server responds with the page content HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html

Hello World
blocks.output: Browser renders 'Hello World' on screen after DNS lookup and HTTP response.

blocks.question: What system translates human-readable domain names (like google.com) into IP addresses?
blocks.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System. It acts like the internet's phonebook.

blocks.value: The HTML Boilerplate Every Page Needs

Every valid HTML5 page starts with a boilerplate. The `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration tells the browser to use modern standards. The `<head>` contains invisible metadata (title, character set, viewport settings), while the `<body>` contains everything the user sees.

Welcome!

This is my first paragraph.
blocks.output: Browser tab shows 'My First Website'. Page displays a large heading and a paragraph.

blocks.question: Which HTML tag contains the page title that appears in the browser tab?
blocks.explanation: The `<title>` tag inside `<head>` sets the text shown in the browser tab and search engine results.

blocks.value: Building Meaningful Page Structure

Semantic tags describe the *meaning* of content, not just its appearance. Using `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<article>`, `<section>`, and `<footer>` helps search engines and screen readers understand your page layout. Avoid using `<div>` for everything.

Home About

Blog Post Title

This is an independent piece of content.

Related links sidebar.

© 2026 My Website
blocks.output: A properly structured page with header navigation, main content area, sidebar, and footer.

blocks.question: Which semantic tag is best for the primary navigation links of a website?
blocks.explanation: `<nav>` is the correct HTML5 semantic element designed specifically for major navigation blocks.

blocks.value: Headings, Paragraphs, Anchors, and Lists

Text is the backbone of the web. Use heading levels `<h1>` through `<h6>` hierarchically. The `<a>` tag creates hyperlinks using the `href` attribute. For lists, use `<ul>` for unordered (bulleted) and `<ol>` for ordered (numbered) lists, with `<li>` as list items.

Main Page Title

Subsection

This is a paragraph with bold and italic text.

Visit MDN Web Docs for more.

My Favorite Languages

  • HTML
  • CSS
  • JavaScript

Steps to Learn

  1. Study HTML
  2. Practice CSS
  3. Build Projects
blocks.output: Rendered page with hierarchical headings, a clickable external link, a bulleted list, and a numbered list.

blocks.question: Which attribute in an `<a>` tag specifies the URL the link should go to?
blocks.explanation: `href` stands for 'hypertext reference' and defines the destination URL of an anchor link.

blocks.value: Adding Visual and Multimedia Content
The `` tag embeds images using the `src` (source) and `alt` (alternative text) attributes. Always include `alt` text for accessibility and SEO. For videos and audio, HTML5 provides `

blocks.output: Page displays an image, a captioned figure, a playable video with controls, and an embedded map.

blocks.question: Which attribute provides descriptive text for screen readers and displays if an image fails to load?
blocks.explanation: The `alt` attribute is critical for accessibility. It describes the image content for visually impaired users and appears as fallback text.

blocks.value: Collecting User Data with Forms

Forms are how websites collect user input. Wrap inputs in a `<form>` tag. Always pair `<label>` with `<input>` using the `for` attribute matching the input's `id`. HTML5 provides many input types like `email`, `tel`, `date`, and `number` that trigger specialized mobile keyboards and built-in validation.

<form action="/register" method="POST">
  <label for="username">Username:</label>
  <input type="text" id="username" name="username" required minlength="3">

  <label for="email">Email:</label>
  <input type="email" id="email" name="email" placeholder="you@example.com" required>

  <label for="password">Password:</label>
  <input type="password" id="password" name="password" minlength="8">

  <label for="birthdate">Birth Date:</label>
  <input type="date" id="birthdate" name="birthdate">

  <label for="plan">Choose Plan:</label>
  <select id="plan" name="plan">
    <option value="free">Free</option>
    <option value="pro">Pro</option>
  </select>

  <label>
    <input type="checkbox" name="terms" required>
    I agree to the terms
  </label>

  <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
</form>
blocks.output: A complete registration form with text, email, password, date picker, dropdown, checkbox, and submit button.

blocks.question: Which input type displays a date picker calendar in modern browsers?
blocks.explanation: `<input type='date'>` renders a native date picker in supporting browsers, improving user experience on both desktop and mobile.

blocks.value: Data Tables and Search Engine Visibility

Use `<table>` for tabular data, never for page layout. Structure tables with `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, and `<tfoot>`. For SEO, include a `<meta name='description'>`, set the viewport for mobile, and use proper heading hierarchies so search engines can index your content correctly.

Product Price Stock
Laptop $999 15
Mouse $25 120
Electronics Shop
blocks.output: A clean data table with headers and body rows. Meta tags help search engines understand and display the page.

blocks.question: Which HTML tag is used to define a row inside a table?
blocks.explanation: `<tr>` stands for 'table row'. It contains `<th>` (header cells) or `<td>` (data cells).

blocks.value: Connecting CSS to HTML and Targeting Elements

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation of HTML. You can write CSS inline (via the `style` attribute), internally (inside a `<style>` tag), or externally (linked `.css` file). Selectors target elements: tag names for all instances, classes (`.`) for reusable groups, and IDs (`#`) for unique elements.

blocks.output: All paragraphs get dark gray text. Elements with class='btn' get padding. The element with id='hero-title' becomes large and purple.

blocks.value:
Welcome

This is a paragraph.
blocks.output: HTML page styled by the external CSS file.

blocks.question: Which CSS selector targets an element with `class='card'`?
blocks.explanation: Classes are selected with a dot prefix (`.card`). IDs use `#` and tag names have no prefix.

parts.partTitle: Part 9: CSS Colors, Fonts & Text Styling

blocks.value: Making Text Beautiful and Readable

CSS offers multiple color formats: named colors (`red`), hex (`#ff0000`), RGB (`rgb(255,0,0)`), and HSL (`hsl(0,100%,50%)`). For fonts, use the `font-family` stack (listing fallbacks), control size with `font-size`, and improve readability with `line-height`. Import custom fonts from Google Fonts using a `<link>` tag.

blocks.output: Body uses Inter font at 16px. Headings are centered, uppercase, indigo-colored. Highlighted text has a light yellow background.

blocks.question: Which CSS property controls the space between lines of text?
blocks.explanation: `line-height` sets the vertical spacing between lines. A value of 1.6 means 1.6 times the font size.

blocks.value: Content, Padding, Border, and Margin

Every HTML element is a rectangular box. The Box Model has four layers: **Content** (text/image inside), **Padding** (space inside the border), **Border** (the edge), and **Margin** (space outside the box). By default, `width` and `height` only apply to the content. Use `box-sizing: border-box` to make width/height include padding and border.

blocks.output: Card has a total visible width of 300px including padding and border. The visual box clearly shows content, padding, border, and margin layers.

blocks.question: Which CSS property makes an element's `width` include its padding and border?
blocks.explanation: `box-sizing: border-box` is the modern standard. It prevents padding and borders from expanding beyond the declared width/height.

blocks.value: Pixels, REM, EM, Percentages, and Viewport Units

Absolute units like `px` are fixed. Relative units scale: `%` is relative to the parent, `em` is relative to the parent font-size, and `rem` is relative to the root (`<html>`) font-size. Viewport units (`vw`, `vh`) are relative to the browser window. For accessible and scalable designs, prefer `rem` for font sizes and `px` for borders.

blocks.output: Container scales with screen but caps at 1200px. Hero section is always half the screen height. Typography scales proportionally with the root font size.

blocks.question: Which unit is always relative to the font-size of the root `<html>` element?
blocks.explanation: `rem` (root em) is relative to the root element's font size, making it predictable across nested components.

blocks.value: Block, Inline, Flex, Grid, and Position Properties

The `display` property defines how an element behaves in layout. `block` takes full width; `inline` flows with text; `inline-block` allows sizing while flowing; `none` hides the element. The `position` property controls placement: `static` (default), `relative` (offset from normal position), `absolute` (relative to nearest positioned ancestor), `fixed` (relative to viewport), and `sticky` (switches between relative and fixed).

blocks.output: Badges sit inline but accept padding. Notifications stick to the top-right of the screen. Avatars shift slightly from their normal position.

blocks.question: Which `position` value keeps an element stuck to the viewport even when the user scrolls?
blocks.explanation: `position: fixed` removes the element from document flow and anchors it to the viewport, so it stays visible during scrolling.

blocks.value: Visual Polish with Colors and Depth

Beyond solid colors, CSS backgrounds can use images, linear gradients, and radial gradients. Borders can have different styles (`solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`) and rounded corners via `border-radius`. The `box-shadow` property adds depth, while `text-shadow` adds depth to typography.

blocks.output: Hero banner has a purple diagonal gradient. Profile cards have rounded corners, subtle borders, and lift up with a deeper shadow on hover.

blocks.question: Which CSS property rounds the corners of an element's border?
blocks.explanation: `border-radius` accepts values in px, %, or rem to round the corners of an element.

blocks.value: Aligning Items Along a Row or Column

Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system perfect for navigation bars, card footers, and centering content. Set `display: flex` on a parent (flex container). Control the main axis with `justify-content` and the cross axis with `align-items`. Use `gap` for spacing between items without margins.

blocks.output: Navbar spreads logo and links apart with vertical centering. Center-box perfectly centers content on screen. Card footer pushes price and button to opposite sides.

blocks.question: Which Flexbox property aligns items along the cross axis (vertically, in a row layout)?
blocks.explanation: `align-items` controls alignment on the cross axis (perpendicular to the main axis). `justify-content` controls the main axis.

blocks.value: Building Complex Page Structures with Rows and Columns

CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system controlling both rows and columns simultaneously. Define tracks with `grid-template-columns` and `grid-template-rows`. Use `fr` (fractional unit) for flexible sizing, `repeat()` for repetition, and `gap` for gutters. Grid is ideal for entire page layouts and card galleries.

blocks.output: Page layout has a full-width header, sidebar on the left, main content area, and full-width footer. Gallery automatically fits as many 280px cards per row as possible.

blocks.question: Which CSS Grid function repeats a track definition a specified number of times?
blocks.explanation: `repeat(3, 1fr)` creates three equal fractional columns. It keeps grid code concise and readable.

blocks.value: Smooth State Changes and 2D/3D Transformations

Transitions animate property changes over time (e.g., changing color on hover). Define the property to animate, duration, timing function, and delay. Transforms modify an element's appearance without affecting document flow — `scale()` for size, `rotate()` for angle, and `translate()` for position.

blocks.output: Buttons smoothly darken and grow slightly on hover. Cards lift up and tilt subtly with an elegant easing curve.

blocks.question: Which CSS property specifies how long a transition animation should take to complete?
blocks.explanation: `transition-duration` sets the time span of the transition, typically in seconds (`0.3s`) or milliseconds (`300ms`).

blocks.value: Creating Complex Multi-Step Animations

While transitions handle simple A-to-B changes, `@keyframes` enable complex animations with multiple steps. Define named keyframes with percentages (0% to 100%), then apply them with the `animation` shorthand property. Control iteration count, direction, and fill mode.

blocks.output: Notifications slide in from the left with a slight overshoot, then settle. Loading dots continuously pulse in size.

blocks.question: Which keyword in a keyframe block represents the final state of the animation?
blocks.explanation: `100%` (or the alias `to`) defines the ending state of the animation. `0%` (or `from`) defines the starting state.

blocks.value: Mobile-First Design and Breakpoints

Responsive design ensures your site looks great on phones, tablets, and desktops. The **Mobile-First** approach writes base styles for small screens, then uses `min-width` media queries to enhance layouts for larger screens. Common breakpoints: 576px (phones), 768px (tablets), 992px (desktops), 1200px (large screens).

blocks.output: On mobile: single column, no sidebar. On tablet: 2-column grid. On desktop: 3-column grid with sidebar visible.

blocks.question: In a mobile-first CSS approach, which media query operator is typically used?
blocks.explanation: Mobile-first means base styles target small screens, and `min-width` media queries progressively enhance the layout as the viewport gets wider.

blocks.value: Connecting JS to HTML and the Browser Console

JavaScript makes web pages interactive. In the browser, JS runs inside a `<script>` tag. Place scripts at the end of the `<body>` so the HTML loads first, or use the `defer` attribute in the `<head>`. The `console.log()` function prints messages to the browser's developer console, essential for debugging.
Hello
blocks.output: Browser console shows three messages. The external app.js loads after HTML parsing due to defer.
External script loaded! A welcome alert appears, then a confirm dialog. The boolean result is logged.

blocks.question: Which `<script>` attribute tells the browser to download the JS file in parallel but execute it only after HTML parsing is complete?
blocks.explanation: `defer` downloads the script without blocking HTML parsing and executes it in order after the DOM is fully built. `async` downloads in parallel but executes immediately, which can interrupt parsing.

blocks.value: Storing and Manipulating Data

Use `let` for variables that change, `const` for values that should never be reassigned, and avoid `var` (it has confusing scope rules). JavaScript has dynamic types: strings, numbers, booleans, null, undefined, objects, and symbols. Operators include arithmetic (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`), comparison (`===`, `!==`, `>`, `<`), and logical (`&&`, `||`, `!`).

blocks.output: Console: false, true, 'Welcome to Web Dev Course! We have 200 students.'

blocks.question: Which declaration keyword creates a variable that cannot be reassigned?
blocks.explanation: `const` prevents reassignment of the variable identifier. Note that for objects and arrays, the contents can still be mutated.

blocks.value: Making Decisions and Repeating Actions

Control flow directs which code runs based on conditions. Use `if/else if/else` for branching. The `switch` statement checks one value against multiple cases. Loops repeat actions: `for` (count-controlled), `while` (condition-controlled), and `for...of` (iterating over arrays).

blocks.output: Grade B, Start of the week, Iteration 1 through 5, Countdown 3 through 1.

blocks.question: Which loop is best for iterating a known number of times with an index variable?
blocks.explanation: The `for` loop is ideal when you know exactly how many iterations you need and want to track an index counter.

blocks.value: Reusable Code Blocks and Variable Visibility

Functions bundle reusable logic. Declare them with the `function` keyword, as expressions, or as arrow functions (`=>`). Arrow functions are concise and preserve the surrounding `this` context. Scope determines where variables are accessible: variables declared inside a function are local to that function; outer variables are accessible inside (closure).

blocks.output: Hello, Alice!, 20, 90, { name: 'Bob', role: 'student' }

blocks.question: Which syntax creates a concise function that implicitly returns a single expression?
blocks.explanation: Arrow functions with no curly braces implicitly return the expression result, making them ideal for short transformations.

parts.partTitle: Part 23: Arrays & Objects for Web Data

blocks.value: Storing and Processing Structured Data

Arrays store ordered lists of values. Objects store key-value pairs. Together they represent real-world data like user lists and product catalogs. Essential array methods for beginners: `push` (add to end), `pop` (remove from end), `indexOf` (find position), `includes` (check existence), and `length` (get count).

blocks.output: 4, 1, 'Alice can be reached at alice@example.com', 'red green'

blocks.question: Which method adds one or more elements to the end of an array?
blocks.explanation: `push()` appends elements to the end. `pop()` removes from the end. `unshift()` adds to the beginning. `shift()` removes from the beginning.

blocks.value: Finding HTML Elements with JavaScript

The DOM (Document Object Model) is a tree representation of your HTML page. JavaScript can query this tree to find elements and read their properties. `document.getElementById()` finds one element by ID. `document.querySelector()` finds the first match for any CSS selector. `document.querySelectorAll()` returns all matches as a NodeList.

Home About Contact
  • Task 1
  • Task 2
  • Task 3

blocks.output: NAV, Home, 3, '0: Task 1', '1: Task 2', '2: Task 3', and the href of the active link.

blocks.question: Which method returns ALL elements matching a CSS selector as a static NodeList?
blocks.explanation: `querySelectorAll('.class')` returns a NodeList of all matching elements, while `querySelector` returns only the first match.

blocks.value: Changing Text, HTML, Styles, and Attributes

Once you select an element, you can modify it. Use `textContent` to change plain text safely (prevents XSS). Use `innerHTML` to inject HTML markup (be cautious with user input). Modify CSS via the `style` property or toggle classes with `classList`. Read and write attributes with `getAttribute` and `setAttribute`.

blocks.output: Heading text updates. Info box gets new HTML content, blue background, and classes toggled. Image source and alt change.

blocks.question: Which property should you use to safely update only the text content of an element without parsing HTML?
blocks.explanation: `textContent` treats the value as plain text, automatically escaping HTML tags. This prevents XSS attacks from untrusted input.

blocks.value: Building Dynamic Pages from Scratch

Instead of writing static HTML, JavaScript can build elements dynamically. Use `document.createElement()` to make a new node, `textContent` or `innerHTML` to fill it, and `appendChild()` or `prepend()` to insert it into the page. For multiple elements, use a **DocumentFragment** to batch insertions and minimize reflows. Remove elements with `remove()`.

blocks.output: New list items are created and appended. First item is removed. 'Urgent Task' is inserted at the top of the list.

blocks.question: Which method creates a new HTML element in memory before it is added to the page?
blocks.explanation: `document.createElement('div')` instantiates a new DOM node in memory. You must then use `appendChild` or similar to actually place it on the page.

blocks.value: User Interaction, Validation, and Persistent Data

Events make pages interactive. `addEventListener` attaches handlers for clicks, input, submissions, and keypresses. Always call `event.preventDefault()` inside form submit handlers to stop page reload. `localStorage` saves strings permanently in the browser (until cleared), while `sessionStorage` clears when the tab closes. Use `JSON.stringify()` and `JSON.parse()` to store objects.

blocks.output: Typing updates greeting live. Submit validates, saves user object to localStorage, and resets form. On reload, saved user is restored and greeted.
Clicking any button with class 'action-btn' inside the container logs its text and toggles an active class.

blocks.question: Which method prevents a form from reloading the page when submitted?
blocks.explanation: `event.preventDefault()` cancels the browser's default action (like form submission reloading the page or a link navigating), allowing JavaScript to handle the event instead.
